summary: Feature Flag Console access broken after SCIM username casing change causing RBAC lookup fail
description: Issue summary: Multiple engineers report 403/Access Denied when opening the Feature Flag Console after a recent Okta SCIM change that normalized usernames to lowercase. Impact: ~12 internal users (engineering and product) cannot access the feature-flag console to review and toggle flags; blocking several onboardings and a small internal experiment rollout. Environment: production console behind SSO via Okta + SCIM-based provisioning. First seen 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC after SCIM change deployed 2026-03-10 07:45 UTC. Expected: users provisioned via SCIM (case-insensitive username match) should inherit RBAC roles and access console. Observed: RBAC lookup fails due to mismatch between stored console principal (TitleCase userPrincipalName) and new SCIM username (lowercase), leading the console to evaluate the user as "unknown" and return 403. No group membership changes reported in Okta.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision or update an Okta user record with a username change that only differs by case (e.g., Aisha.Kapoor@redwood.com -> aisha.kapoor@redwood.com)
2) Wait for SCIM sync window (or trigger manual sync)
3) Login to console via Okta SSO
4) Attempt to navigate to /console/feature-flags or open the feature flag UI
5) Observe 403 and 'Access Denied' modal.
Note: reproduces reliably when the console principal record still references the older-cased identity.
investigation: Initial triage by Support (Luis) confirmed error path in console auth logs pointing to RBAC lookup failure: 'principal lookup no-match: username="aisha.kapoor@redwood.com" expected="Aisha.Kapoor@redwood.com"'. SCIM provisioner logs (provisioner-02) show successful PATCH that normalized userPrincipalName to lower case at 2026-03-10T07:44:12Z. Console's RBAC cache retains the old principal key and does strict string equality when resolving identities. We confirmed at least 12 principals in the console DB with mixed-case stored usernames; SCIM syncs now produce lowercase. Hypothesis: SCIM normalizer change intended to enforce lowercase broke backward compatibility with console RBAC keying. No ACL/group changes were observed in Okta. Session tokens created before the change remain valid but new sessions are evaluated against new SCIM usernames and denied. Logs referenced: auth-console-prod.log lines 4782-4800 (attached), provisioner-02.log lines 213-218. Related PR that changed normalizer: provisioner PR #412.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:02 — Luis Ortega: Confirmed scope and reproduced with test account. Creating ticket and pinging IAM and Console owners.

2026-03-10 10:15 — Priya Nair (IAM): We intentionally landed lowercase normalization to match external identity providers; didn't realize downstream strict-equality assumptions. Adding provisioner PR link.

2026-03-10 11:05 — Marcos Li (Console): Console RBAC lookup uses username string as primary key in cache. We can change to case-insensitive compare as a short-term fix, but need to decide canonicalization strategy for DB keys.
2026-03-11 08:30 — Aisha Kapoor: I lost access to a/12 feature flags that I needed for an experiment. Temporarily using CLI tool with admin token as workaround requested.

2026-03-12 14:40 — Luis Ortega: Rolled a temporary mitigation script to backfill console principal records to lowercase for impacted users (see runbook link). Investigating safe rollout for bulk reconciliation.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-12): one-off backfill script updated 12 affected console principal records to normalized lowercase username; users regained access. Longer-term fixes: (1) Console change to perform case-insensitive identity resolution and record a canonical username on first login (PR #589 pending review). (2) Update SCIM provisioner to publish canonical_username attribute and add a migration runbook. Follow-up items created: INT-64200 (RBAC canonical key migration plan), provisioner PR #412 closed and replaced with #421 to include canonical attribute. No customer-facing impact.
postmortem_actions: - Add automated reconciliation job to run daily for 30 days to catch mismatches. - Update RBAC layer to accept case-insensitive lookups and persist canonical_username. - Add integration test for SCIM normalization behavior. - Communicate change in internal release notes and IAM changelog. Assigned owners: Marcos (Console), Priya (IAM), Luis (Support).
workaround: Admin can run temporary backfill script (internal-only) to rewrite console principal keys to lowercase for specific users. Support executed this for the 12 affected users and validated access. Steps and script are documented in the linked runbook.
notes: This ticket is internal; prioritize the RBAC canonical key fix ahead of the next SCIM deployment. Consider a short freeze on additional SCIM normalizer changes until migration path is in place.
